The core safety rules

Clay shooting is a very safe sport, but only because everyone keeps a few simple habits. Learn them before your first shot. Follow them always, even when you are sure the gun is empty.

Safety: The muzzle, the open front end of the barrel, always points in a safe direction. On the stand that means towards the targets, down the range (out over the field where the targets fly). Off the stand it points straight up or straight down. Never point a gun at a person, even unloaded, even as a joke.

The gun stays open whenever you are not shooting. On an over-and-under (two barrels, one above the other) you “break” it: the barrels tip down from the stock. Then anyone can see that the chambers (where the cartridges sit) are empty. On a semi-automatic you pull the action (the moving part that loads the cartridge) back and leave it open. An open gun tells everyone nearby that it is safe.

Any gun is treated as dangerous, even when it is empty. Off the stand it is carried open: an over-and-under broken (opened at the hinge) and resting on your forearm, a semi-automatic with the action open. The muzzles point straight up or straight down. Slings (straps for carrying a gun on the shoulder) are not allowed. When nobody is using it, the gun stands upright in a gun rack. Nobody touches another shooter’s gun without permission.

Cartridges go into the gun only on the stand, with the muzzles pointing down the range, and only when the referee or instructor allows it. A semi-automatic holds no more than two. Before turning round on the stand, the shooter opens the gun and takes out all cartridges, fired or not. During the target presentation, when the targets are thrown so the squad can see where they fly, guns are open and empty. The same applies during any stop. Guns are closed again only when the referee allows it.

Compak® Sporting

In Compak® Sporting, load only on your own station (your numbered shooting place), with the gun open and pointing out over the field. Keep the barrels inside the angle limiter, the frame around the station that stops them swinging too far to the side, up or down. Close the gun only when it is your turn.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 24 · Safe procedure on the shooting position

Safety: When anyone calls “Stop!” or “Cease fire!”, or the shooting ground gives its own stop signal, everyone stops at once. Open the gun, take out the cartridges and wait. Close it again only when the referee or instructor allows. If you see a danger, such as a person in front of the stand, call “Stop!” yourself.

Safety: If the gun fails to fire (a misfire), stay in place with the gun pointing down the range. Do not open it or touch the safety catch until the referee, or in training the instructor, has checked it. One reason: a cartridge can fire a moment late, a hang fire. This is a safety rule and a scoring rule at once. If you open the gun or touch the safety catch before the referee’s check, the target is scored as a miss (zero).

Safety: A thunderstorm needs extra care. In a sudden downpour or storm the referee may pause shooting; in Compak® Sporting the Head Referee decides. During any pause guns are open and empty. With lightning nearby, do not stand in the open holding a gun: take shelter in a building.

These habits are written in the FITASC rules and in the house rules of grounds. In training the instructor watches over them, and in competition the referee. What matters most is that they become your own habits.

Key points

  • The muzzle points in a safe direction, never at people
  • Off the stand: gun open, empty, muzzles up or down, no slings
  • Load only on the stand, pointing down the range, with permission; semi-auto max 2
  • After a misfire: stay put, do not open, wait for the referee
  • On a stop command: open the gun, remove cartridges, wait

Did you know?

A safety catch is no substitute for an open gun: the open gun is the main sign of safety at a ground.

Stand Talk

  • Coach Guns open and empty between stands, please.

    Meaning: Walking to the next stand, the gun is broken with no cartridges inside.

  • Coach Break your gun and show me it’s clear.

    Meaning: Open the gun (not damage it!) so I can see the chambers are empty.

  • Coach Don’t load until you’re on the stand and I say so.

    Meaning: No cartridges in the gun while walking or waiting.

  • Coach Muzzles down when you turn round.

    Meaning: Never let the barrels point at people, even with an open gun.

  • Referee Stop! Stop! Guns open!

    Meaning: Emergency stop: stop shooting, open the gun, wait.

For the interpreter
  • When anyone shouts “Stop!” or “Cease fire!”, everyone stops at once and opens the gun. Do not translate this into a sentence: repeat “Stop!” loudly in your guests’ language and check that their guns are open. If a guest turns towards you with a gun to ask something, point the muzzles down with a gesture first and translate afterwards.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Where may you load the gun?

    1. Anywhere at the ground, if the gun points at the ground
    2. Only on the stand, pointing down the range, once shooting is allowed
    3. On the way to the stand, so you are ready when called
    Answer

    Only on the stand, pointing down the range, once shooting is allowed

    Cartridges go in only on the stand, with the gun pointing down the range, after the referee or instructor allows shooting.

  2. What must you do before turning round on the stand?

    1. Open the gun and take out all cartridges, fired or not
    2. Put the safety catch on and keep the gun closed
    3. Take out only the unfired cartridges, then close the gun
    Answer

    Open the gun and take out all cartridges, fired or not

    You turn round only with the gun open and empty; a safety catch is no substitute for an open gun.

  3. The gun clicks but does not fire. What should the shooter do?

    1. Open it at once to see what went wrong
    2. Turn round and show the gun to the coach
    3. Stay put, gun down the range, and wait for the referee
    4. Put the safety on and call for the target again
    Answer

    Stay put, gun down the range, and wait for the referee

    Both rulebooks require the shooter to stay put until the referee inspects; opening or touching the safety first scores zero.
